summary: Everything the developer workplaces carry, in one image: PHP, Java, Flutter, the Python and Flutter version managers, a database and the native build toolchain. The all-rounder — nothing here has to be fetched first.

tools.name: flutter
tools.note: in /opt/flutter and on your PATH, warmed up for web builds. This is the baseline — you do not download it. The version is the one the image was built with, so `flutter --version` is the authority, not this line.

tools.name: fvm
tools.note: only for a project that pins another Flutter version: `fvm use <version>` puts it in ~/fvm and it stays there

tools.name: php
tools.note: with xml, mbstring, curl, zip, gd, ldap, sqlite3, mysql, pgsql, bcmath, intl, and pcov as the coverage driver

tools.name: openjdk
tools.note: JAVA_HOME=/opt/java; gradlew downloads its own Gradle

tools.name: build-essential, python3
tools.note: so npm packages with a native part (sharp, bcrypt, node-sass) build instead of failing halfway

tools.name: uv
tools.note: Python interpreters, version from .python-version; they land in ~/.local/share/uv

tools.name: chromium
tools.note: used by the browser plugin, headless; also what `flutter run -d chrome` needs

tools.name: mariadb-server
tools.note: for test suites that need a real database. No systemd here and you are not root: initialise a data directory in your home once (mariadb-install-db --datadir=~/.local/share/mariadb) and start mariadbd yourself against it. Put that directory in a place you are willing to lose — it is scratch, not memory.

sdk_dirs.fvm: ~/fvm — only Flutter versions you asked for yourself. The baseline SDK is NOT here, it is in the image.
sdk_dirs.uv: ~/.local/share/uv — Python interpreters. uv fetches the version a project asks for.

notes: This workplace has every toolchain there is here. If something seems to be missing, look again before you fetch it — Java, Flutter and a database are all present, and a copy in your home is written back after every run.
No Android SDK. A build that has to produce an APK needs one, and asking for it is the way to get it — do not unpack platform-tools into your home.
You are not root and apt is not available to you. If a tool is missing, say so instead of building a way around it — that is a request, not a defeat.
